clue.text: Inevitably salesman returns to power

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
force and power are synonyms

explanation.surface: A salesman who left keeps coming back to positions of power, as if it were bound to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inevitably' sits at the front looking like an adverb setting the scene, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce is a slightly old-fashioned adverb meaning by necessity, unavoidably, as things must be.

clue.text: What the profitable hen did (likewise, we hear, the early bird)

indicators.note: what we hear is a word judged by its sound, so the spelling may differ

parts.note: Early Bird was the 1965 communications satellite that passed television signals across the Atlantic

explanation.surface: A productive hen laid egg after egg, and so did the proverbial early bird, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The early bird is not the proverbial one catching the worm but the satellite Early Bird, which relayed signals; that sounds the same as RELAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A profitable hen keeps producing eggs, so she laid again and again, which is re-laid.

clue.text: How hot water can be used for swelling

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bubbling at boiling point

definitions.note: a description of where the water goes, not a synonym
definitions.meaning: second meaning: placed upon a boil, a painful swelling, as an old hot compress would be

explanation.surface: Household advice on using hot water to treat an inflamed swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Water at a rolling simmer is said to be bubbling away, while a boil is a skin swelling that a poultice sits upon.

clue.text: Indispensable parts of building at an angle

definitions.text: Indispensable parts of building at an angle

parts.note: surface reading: the essential foundations of any enterprise
setter's reading: the literal blocks laid where two walls of a building meet

explanation.surface: Talk of the essential elements that hold a construction together at its angles.
explanation.definitionFit: The figurative sense is a basic essential element; the literal sense is masonry laid where two walls join.

clue.text: So crafty was Dawkins

definitions.note: a nickname, the word in the Dodger's title
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Jack Dawkins is Dickens's ... Dodger in Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: Someone called Dawkins was remarkably cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawkins here is not the scientist but Jack Dawkins, the young pickpocket known as the Artful Dodger.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means cunning or skilful in a sly way, and it forms the first half of the pickpocket's nickname.

clue.text: Rover wrecked on a rock

parts.note: surface reading: a wandering ship or dog lost on rocks
setter's reading: the pirate called the Rover in Southey's ballad The Inchcape Rock, who drowned on the reef whose warning bell he had cut away

explanation.surface: A wanderer comes to grief on a rock at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Southey's ballad tells how the pirate, Sir Ralph the Rover, removed the bell from the Inchcape Rock and was later wrecked there himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirate's given name in the ballad is the answer, since he is always styled Sir Ralph the Rover.

clue.text: This kind of medicine is legal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: medicine applied to crime and courts, as in post-mortems
second meaning: relating to courts of law

explanation.surface: Reassurance that a certain sort of drug is perfectly lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective originally means belonging to courts or public debate, and names the branch of medicine serving criminal investigation.

clue.text: French connexions, booked as dangerous

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a borrowed French word for links or affairs

definitions.note: points to a book title, Les Liaisons dangereuses
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Laclos's novel Les ... dangereuses gives them that adjective in its title

explanation.surface: Contacts in France have been officially flagged as hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booked' means written into a book: the 1782 novel by Choderlos de Laclos.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is French for links or affairs, used in English for both, and appears in the novel's title.

clue.text: Yon — Highland lass" (Wordsworth)

parts.note: surface reading: a quotation with a word missing
setter's reading: the source is a famous 1805 poem about a girl reaping and singing alone, whose title and opening lines hold the gap's word

explanation.surface: A line of Wordsworth with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem begins 'Behold her, single in the field, Yon ___ Highland Lass!' and its title gives the word away.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adjective means alone, describing the girl reaping by herself in the Scottish field.

clue.text: Girl in service

definitions.note: describes where the hymn is sung rather than naming it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the hymn of praise sung in the Mass or a church service

explanation.surface: A young woman who works as a domestic servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In service' suggests domestic work; here the service is a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name and also the Latin hymn Gloria in excelsis sung during worship.

clue.text: Extol one of Fuller's subjects-that's laudable

parts.note: to extol is to speak highly of
Thomas Fuller wrote The History of the Worthies of England, so each subject is one of them

explanation.surface: Speaking well of someone from a biographical collection seems a commendable thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Fuller was a 17th-century clergyman whose great work profiled the notable people of each English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something deserving approval and commendation, the adjective and its longer synonym.

clue.text: It's nothing to collapse an arch

parts.note: O looks like zero
a floor or roof that gives collapses under weight

explanation.surface: An arch is so weak that it falls down easily.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture this word names a pointed Gothic arch or a diagonal rib of a vault.

clue.text: Listener calls for head-set parts

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens
to phone someone is to call them

explanation.surface: Someone listening rings up to ask for spare pieces of their headset.
explanation.definitionFit: A headset consists of two small speakers worn over each side of the head, joined by a band.

clue.text: Make-up of government principles

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person's physical or mental composition
second meaning: the fundamental laws by which a state is run

explanation.surface: A phrase describing how a government is structured by its rules.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers bodily health or temperament and also a nation's founding framework of laws.

clue.text: Unscrupulous sort of lunatic, he?

indicators.note: a sort of something is a version of it, so the letters are reworked into another form

parts.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: A question whether a madman counts as a dishonest kind of person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone without moral principles, prepared to act dishonestly or wrongly.

clue.text: Jack backs Civil Service on dock strike initially, but runs away

parts.note: Jack and AB, able seaman, are both words for a sailor

indicators.note: to back is to move in reverse, so the abbreviation is read the other way

parts.note: standard abbreviation
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words it follows

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A sailor supports the civil servants during a dockers' strike, then flees.
explanation.walkthrough: CS reversed is SC: AB + SC + ON + D + S makes ABSCONDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to flee secretly, especially to escape custody or responsibility.

clue.text: Try heather for dobbin's accommodation

parts.note: to have a stab is to have a try
ling is the common heather of moorland

explanation.surface: Someone suggests putting heather down as bedding for the old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Dobbin is a traditional pet name for a farm horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Housing provided for horses is called by this noun, from the building where they are kept.

clue.text: It permits flow of liquid assets

definitions.text: It permits flow of liquid assets

parts.note: surface reading: finance, cash that can be moved freely
setter's reading: drinks, quite literally valuable liquids, released by a gadget

explanation.surface: Something in banking that allows money to circulate.
explanation.definitionFit: The gadget removes caps from drinks containers, letting the precious liquid be poured out.

clue.text: O, short, nothing but gas

definitions.note: the letter is the abbreviated form, a description rather than a synonym
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the element whose chemical symbol is the single letter O
second meaning: the colourless gas that makes up a fifth of the air

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that something amounting to zero is just hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: O reads first as zero, which is why 'nothing' follows so naturally, but here it is the chemical symbol, short for the element.
explanation.definitionFit: The element breathed by animals is a gas at room temperature, and chemists abbreviate it with the single letter O.

clue.text: Don takes taxi to go abroad, nothing to it

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
aller is the French verb meaning to go
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A university lecturer catches a cab to travel overseas without luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' suggests a university teacher, but here it is the Spanish title for a gentleman. 'Abroad' asks for the foreign word.
explanation.definitionFit: A caballero is a Spanish gentleman or knight, and Don is the Spanish honorific for such a man.

clue.text: Heal breach with top Red composer

indicators.note: a breach is a break, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the top of a word written down the grid is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A plea to mend a split with a senior Communist musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian composer of the operetta The Merry Widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár wrote light operettas, so he is a well-known writer of music.

clue.text: Hospital X-ray treatment for a rock-rabbit

parts.note: H is the map symbol for a hospital

indicators.note: treating something works it over, so the letters are processed into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: A sick rabbit is sent to the hospital for a scan.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyrax is a small furry African mammal that lives among rocks and looks like a rabbit or guinea pig.

clue.text: Calls from paddock for gin she's mixing

indicators.note: mixing a drink stirs its contents together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Shouts come from a field while a woman makes up a gin cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses in a paddock make a high whinnying cry, and that sound is the plural noun here.

clue.text: Farm-workers thus fiddling their cards?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: piling hay or sheaves into ricks
second meaning: secretly arranging a pack so the deal favours you

explanation.surface: Labourers on a farm caught cheating at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Labourers pile up bales into a heap, and a cheat arranges the pack beforehand in a rigged order.

clue.text: Make us return gay, having eaten right sweet

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: whatever has eaten something holds it inside

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring us back cheerful once we have had the right food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is only a lead-in; the turning back acts on 'us' alone, and the abbreviation for right sits inside 'gay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tasting heavily of sugar is sweet, so the adjectives match closely.

clue.text: Flower in an endless series — so be it

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a cycle is a series of events that repeats
amen is Hebrew for so be it, said at the end of prayers

explanation.surface: Accepting resignedly that a flower blooms in a never-ending round.
explanation.walkthrough: CYCLE loses its last letter to give CYCL, then AMEN completes CYCLAMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The cyclamen is a plant with swept-back pink or white petals, popular as a houseplant.
